module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 1.74 (Minimal topological groups)

by V. P. Platonov

Describe all "minimal topological groups", that is, non-discrete Hausdorff
topological groups all of whose proper closed subgroups are discrete. The
minimal locally compact groups can be described without much effort, but the
problem is probably complicated in the general case.

A Tarski monster group equipped with a non-discrete Hausdorff group topology
is a minimal topological group in this sense, since all its proper subgroups
are finite (hence discrete in any Hausdorff group topology). Such topologizable
Tarski monsters exist by a theorem of Klyachko, Olshanskii and Osin.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v40)
- A. A. Klyachko, A. Yu. Olshanskii, D. V. Osin, *On topologizable and
  non-topologizable groups*, Topology Appl. 160 (2013), 2104–2120,
  [arXiv:1210.7895](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.7895), Theorem 1.4.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Kourovka.«1.74»

/--
A minimal topological group in Platonov's sense: a non-discrete Hausdorff
topological group all of whose proper closed subgroups are discrete.
-/
def IsMinimalTopologicalGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] : Prop :=
  IsTopologicalGroup G ∧ T2Space G ∧ ¬ DiscreteTopology G ∧
    ∀ H : Subgroup G, H ≠ ⊤ → IsClosed (H : Set G) → DiscreteTopology H

/--
Describe all minimal topological groups, that is, all non-discrete Hausdorff
topological groups whose proper closed subgroups are all discrete.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka_1_74 :
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G],
      IsMinimalTopologicalGroup G ↔
        (answer(sorry) : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G], Prop) G := by
  sorry

/--
A Tarski monster group: an infinite group in which every non-trivial proper
subgroup has order a fixed prime $p$.
-/
def IsTarskiMonster (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  Infinite G ∧ ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧
    ∀ H : Subgroup G, H ≠ ⊥ → H ≠ ⊤ → Nat.card H = p

/--
There exists a Tarski monster group that admits a non-discrete Hausdorff group
topology. This follows from Theorem 1.4 of Klyachko, Olshanskii and Osin, which
gives a topologizable Tarski monster of every sufficiently large odd exponent $n$;
taking $n$ to be a prime $p$ makes every non-trivial proper subgroup cyclic of
order $p$. Any such group is a minimal topological group.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka_1_74.variants.tarski_monster : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : TopologicalSpace G),
      IsTarskiMonster G ∧ IsTopologicalGroup G ∧ T2Space G ∧
      ¬ DiscreteTopology G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«1.74»

reformulations.difference: The source (Kourovka 1.74) defines minimal topological groups as "non-discrete groups all of whose closed subgroups are discrete". The Lean definition (used by `Kourovka.«1.74».kourovka_1_74`) adds `T2Space G` (Hausdorff). It also quantifies only over proper closed subgroups (`H ≠ ⊤`). The module and theorem docstrings include both words silently, as if they were part of the problem text.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (i) "Proper" is forced. G is itself a closed subgroup and it is non-discrete, so the literal reading describes the empty class. Proved in Lean: `¬ (¬ DiscreteTopology G ∧ ∀ H : Subgroup G, IsClosed (H : Set G) → DiscreteTopology H)`, since `↥⊤` is homeomorphic to G. (ii) Hausdorff is the standard convention for this notion. Morris (Bull. Aust. Math. Soc. 34 (1986) 473–475, zbMATH 0588.22005) settles the locally compact case in exactly these terms: "a non-discrete locally compact Hausdorff group has each of its proper closed subgroups … discrete iff it is … the circle group or the group of real numbers". KOO likewise assume all topological groups are Hausdorff. Dropping T2 changes the class only by a trivial family. Proved in Lean: `IsMinimalNoT2 G ↔ IsMinimalTopologicalGroup G ∨ (IsTopologicalGroup G ∧ IndiscreteTopology G ∧ Nontrivial G)`, where `IsMinimalNoT2` is the definition without `T2Space`. Proof idea: closure{1} is a closed subgroup with the indiscrete subspace topology. If it is proper, it must be discrete, hence trivial; then {1} is closed, so G is T1 and hence T2. Otherwise G is indiscrete. So a description of either class gives a description of the other, and the "describe all" problem is the same.

review.notes:
No misformalizations found. Declarations checked: `IsMinimalTopologicalGroup`, `kourovka_1_74`, `IsTarskiMonster` and `kourovka_1_74.variants.tarski_monster` (all in `Kourovka.«1.74»`).

Lean experiments (all compiled, in /workspace/review):
- `DiscreteTopology ↥H` uses the induced topology; checked with `rfl`.
- `IsMinimalTopologicalGroup (Multiplicative ℝ)` holds. So the definition is satisfiable and agrees with Morris's (1986) classification of the locally compact case (ℝ and the circle).
- The literal reading without "proper" is unsatisfiable.
- Dropping T2 adds exactly the indiscrete groups with at least two elements (see the reformulation).
- A group with `IsTarskiMonster G`, a Hausdorff group topology and a non-discrete topology satisfies `IsMinimalTopologicalGroup G`. The variant's existential is therefore equivalent to "some Tarski monster is a minimal topological group", as its docstring claims.
- `pp.explicit` confirms that the variant's instances are the bound existential ones.

`kourovka_1_74` uses the repository's standard "describe/determine" pattern, `∀ G, P G ↔ (answer(sorry) : … → Prop) G`, as in Erdős 592 and 596. The fact that the tautological answer proves it is accepted by CONTRIBUTING.md. The `research open` tag matches the source: the latest Kourovka version (Sept 2026) still lists 1.74 as unsolved, with no comment. Morris–Obraztsov (1998) only construct examples of non-discrete groups with all proper subgroups discrete; that is not a description.

On the variant: KOO define a Tarski Monster as a finitely generated infinite simple group whose proper subgroups are all finite cyclic. Theorem 1.4 gives topologizable ones of every sufficiently large odd exponent n. Taking n to be a large prime p gives the file's fixed-prime definition, since every nontrivial proper subgroup then has order p. The variant is a correct corollary, so `answer(True)` and `research solved` are right. The earlier Morris–Obraztsov examples have unbounded exponent and would not meet the file's definition, so citing KOO is correct. The theorem number and journal reference in the file are both correct.

Optional documentation suggestion (not a defect): the docstrings present "Hausdorff" and "proper" as part of the problem statement. The source text has neither word. A one-line note that these are the standard reading (as in Morris 1986) would make the docstring match the source exactly.

I read the problem text in the latest arXiv version (v46) rather than the cited v40. Both belong to the same 21st issue (January 2026), and the text of this 1965 problem is unchanged. I could not reach the Russian original.
